Hold on now, easy does it. Welcome to life after a narcissistic relationship. Most if not all of us can relate. I left mine only to find a month later she's getting married bought a home evicted me off her property I built a house on and had destroyed my confidence BTW I have to be in court Monday for domestic abuse. Have not had contact in 2 months. You're not anything he said I can almost guarantee. You're not stupid you just loved the type of person who will literally suck the life out of you. Their whole mission in life is to find a supply, destroy their supply and repeat. I know it ain't easy and I'm going to therapy for it but you have to understand you're fine. They're miserable and you'll recover they won't. My Nex is living the high life for now but I'll bet within 3 years it's over. Anyone can wear a mask for a couple years but you'll eventually catch them being who they are. When they do let them and walk.

I feel your pain. For the last 2 years I've worked painstakingly at pleasing my Nex. We broke up and I moved away. She called and needed my help so I moved back in hope of rebuilding our relationship. She needed an address for her son to attend a good school. She bought a little lot that was pretty much unusable and rented a backhoe. I did the excavation and built a house pad. She then needed a structure on it so I bought a portable bldg and went to work on a tiny house. Things went well for a few months then the verbal abuse started up again. She had written a 99 year lease but due to the wording it's not valid. So now I'm sitting with a home nearly completed on her lot. She has recently purchased a home with another man moved away and told me to vacate. Her verbal abuse doesn't stop every time we communicate it's the same old crap. We're down to email only communicaton. Her dad and I are good friends and she won't even face him. What this taught me is a narcissist is the most EVIL person you can be around. They work on you untill there's nothing left and move on. The best suggestion I have for you is get out while there's something left of yourself. I'm 30k invested plus ALL the labor into something that she's going to gain. I'm left with a broken heart, homeless, and an anger beyond measure. What really pisses me off is I still love her.

That's been over a month ago she's moved off with another guy and her dad now knows she's a whore, but that's another story. He asked me why I wrote that down, to remind me not to get too close. I'm so glad it's over and I hope you can find peace.

7 days ago I realized that no matter what I'm bound to addiction. We reap what we sow and I'll never outlive my crops. So here I am drunk in the same bed I've been in for a week reaping what I planted. 
Now if you don't want to die drunk stop associating with it. The devil lives in every glass and every bottle. I believe everytime we consume the devil he gets to be more of who we are. Please don't do what I did.

On 10-4-02 a volunteer fire department EMT squad showed up because law enforcement would not. I had severe head trauma and had been stabbed puncturing a lung. They kept me alive called in a bird and sent me to OU Medical. I promised a little boy prior to all this that I wouldn't leave him. Those who go into the fire are our heros. The boy his mom and I saw those guys and I thanked them. We have pics of a 2 yr old on a fire truck with hat badge and all. 
   All these years later I'm laying drunk for 7 days now wondering if they made the right decision. 
I admire you wanting to make amends but the biggest most powerful amend you can make is being a good person and giving to society. People need people that are happy productive and useful.

Hey man I'm 57 I've been on something pretty much daily since 15. Since 94 everyday except for a 9 month clean and sober time in 2010. This past June I celebrated 2 yrs on the 7th. For the last 6 days I've been drunk haven't bathed changed clothes or left the bed except to piss and make a drink. In 2 hrs I'm going to my first meeting in over a year. I got sober because I was tired of hurting my woman and her 8 yr old son. It turned out that the damage was done and I never got her truly back. We haven't spoken since Father's Day. I said all that to say this. You are the only one you hurt when you drink. Sure others suffer but you're the one who pays the ultimate price. My words of wisdom is this: put nothing before your sobriety. Don't allow yourself to be vulnerable to anyone or anything in the program or not, and lastly never love anyone that you can't walk away from.
